Updated: `r Sys.Date()`

The figures of the report, in English. This is the English version of
[Tuottavuuslautakunnan raportti 2026](board_2026.qmd): the same figures with the
same file names, but the labels and the text are in English. Titles, subtitles
and sources are text above the figure, not part of the figure itself, and every
figure is also saved as a png and a pdf in a folder named after the year of
publication. The files are written to `figures/en/<year>/` instead of
`figures/<year>/`, so that the two language versions never overwrite each
other.

In the folder `figures/en/captioned/<year>/` each figure is also saved as a
standalone 16 x 12 cm png with the title, subtitle and source drawn on the
image; it is meant to be used without the running text of the report. In the
folder `figures/en/data/<year>/` the data behind each figure is saved in a wide
format as an xlsx file, one column per series.

## The data in brief

The numbers come from the combined dataset of the package: EU and EEA countries
from Eurostat's national accounts, the rest from the OECD productivity database.
Chain-linked volumes are not additive, so industries are summed through series
in the previous year's prices and chained again — this is how the business
sector (NACE B–N excluding real estate) is built as well. For the OECD
countries, hours worked and persons employed are derived back from value added
and labour productivity, because the database holds neither hours nor persons on
their own. The cost competitiveness indicators are relative to 17 peer
countries, weighted with ECFIN's trade weights.

In more detail: how the data is built and what the measures are in
[Talouskasvu ja tuottavuus](main.qmd), the difference in hours worked between
the sources in [Työtunnit: Eurostat ja OECD](tyotunnit.qmd) and the definitions
of unit labour costs in [Kustannuskilpailukyky](competitiveness.qmd) (those
articles are in Finnish). The code of the dataset is `data-raw/data_main.R`.

```{r}
#| label: setup
# library(fiprod)

if (interactive()) devtools::load_all(".") else library(fiprod)

library(tidyverse)
library(ggcustom)
library(pttdatahaku)


set_gg(theme_fpb(base_size = 11))

y_log_breaks <- scales::breaks_pretty(n = 8)

# The vintage data does not update unless the data files are deleted first.
vintage_year <- 2026

# Year of publication. The figures are written to figures/en/<year>/, size
# 13.5 x 8.5 cm. The other defaults of the saving (size, resolution, format,
# folder) are the defaults of save_fig() and can be changed here in the same
# call. The folder is not the one the Finnish version writes to, so the two
# language versions live side by side.
report_year <- 2026

set_fig_defaults(dir = file.path("figures", "en"), year = report_year)

# Besides save_fig(), every figure is also saved as a standalone png with the
# title, subtitle and source drawn on the image (save_fig_captioned()). It is
# meant to be used without the running text of the report, so it is bigger
# (16 x 12 cm) and goes to a folder of its own, figures/en/captioned/<year>/,
# so that it does not overwrite the files of save_fig().
set_fig_captioned_defaults(dir = file.path("figures", "en", "captioned"), year = report_year)

# The data of each figure is also saved in a wide format as an xlsx file in the
# folder figures/en/data/<year>/ (save_fig_data()).
set_fig_data_defaults(dir = file.path("figures", "en", "data"), year = report_year)

dat_gdp_main <- load_dat("dat_gdp_main", vintage = vintage_year)

dat_gva_ind_comb <- load_dat("dat_gva_ind_comb", vintage = vintage_year)

geos <- rev(c(
  "Finland"       = "FI",
  "Euro area"     = "EA20",
  "Sweden"        = "SE",
  "Denmark"       = "DK",
  "Germany"       = "DE",
  "France"        = "FR",
  "USA"           = "US",
  "other"         = "Other"
))

geos_width <- set_names(if_else(geos %in% c("FI"), 2, 1.3), names(geos))
geos_colour <- set_names(c("grey80", rev(ggcustom_pal(length(geos) -1, "fpb"))), names(geos)) # grey for the "other" group


# geos_name <- set_names(names(geos), geos)

# Cost competitiveness

dat_ulc_comp     <- load_dat("dat_ulc_comp", vintage = vintage_year)
dat_oecd_pdb_ulc <- load_dat("dat_oecd_pdb_ulc", vintage = vintage_year)

start_year <- 2000

# Reference period of the index: the average of 2000 - latest = 100, as in the
# report
mean_range <- start_year:lubridate::year(max(dat_ulc_comp$time))



# Picks one or more indicators in a wide shape and rebases the index
pick <- function(vars_keep, col = "rel", geo_keep = "FI") {
  dat_ulc_comp |>
    filter(
      geo %in% geo_keep,
      vars %in% vars_keep,
      lubridate::year(time) >= start_year) |>
    select(time, geo, vars, extended, values = all_of(col)) |>
    mutate(values = rebase_index(values, time, mean_range), .by = c(geo, vars)) |>
    mutate(vars = fct_recode(factor(vars, levels = vars_keep), !!!vars_keep))
}

sub_ind <- paste0("Index, average ", min(mean_range), "–", max(mean_range), " = 100")

# Period of the public sector comparison: the average growth rates are taken
# over these years
public_period <- 1998:2023
public_period_lab <- paste0(min(public_period), "–", max(public_period))

# Figures of chapters 3, 4.2, 5 and 6
#
# The series come ready calculated from Excel files (data-raw/rap_2026/Luku3.xlsx,
# Luku4_2.xlsx, Luku5.xlsx and Luku6.xlsx), which are read by the scripts
# data-raw/read_luku3.R, read_luku4_2.R, read_luku5.R and read_luku6.R. A vintage
# is not needed, because the Excel files are the files of this report itself and
# do not update from an interface.
dat_luku3_2026 <- load_dat("dat_luku3_2026")
dat_luku4_2_2026 <- load_dat("dat_luku4_2_2026")
dat_luku5_2026 <- load_dat("dat_luku5_2026")
dat_luku6_2026 <- load_dat("dat_luku6_2026")

# The names of the series, panels and categories in the Excel files are in
# Finnish. This translates them, the names of the levels of the factors only,
# so that the figures and the data files made from them are in English. The
# names are the Finnish ones as they stand in the files; a name that is not
# here (country codes, years) is left as it is.
fi_en <- c(

  "Työn tuottavuus" = "Labour productivity",

  "Majoitus- ja ravitsemistoiminta" = "Accommodation and food services",
  "Kiinteistöala" = "Real estate",
  "Asiantuntijapalvelut" = "Professional services",
  "Tukipalvelut" = "Support services",
  # figure 9, industries
  "Tutkimus- ja kehittämistoiminta (M72)" = "Research and development (M72)",
  "Lakiasiain- ja laskentatoimen palvelut (M69)" = "Legal and accounting services (M69)",
  "Tietopalvelut (J63)" = "Information services (J63)",
  "Ohjelmistojen suunnittelu ja valmistus (J62010)" = "Computer programming (J62010)",
  "Hotellit (I55101)" = "Hotels (I55101)",
  "Varastointi ja liikennettä palveleva toiminta (H52)" = "Warehousing and transport support activities (H52)",
  "Tieliikenteen tavarankuljetus (H49410)" = "Freight transport by road (H49410)",
  "Moottoriajoneuvojen huolto ja korjaus (G45201)" = "Maintenance and repair of motor vehicles (G45201)",
  # figure 10, sources of labour productivity growth
  "Jatkavat yritykset, ei yritysjärjestelyjä" = "Continuing firms, no restructuring",
  "Yritysostoja tehneet jatkavat yritykset" = "Continuing firms that made acquisitions",
  "Aito markkinoille tulo ja poistuminen" = "Genuine entry and exit",
  "Yritysjärjestelyihin liittyvä markkinoille tulo ja poistuminen" = "Entry and exit related to restructuring",
  "Työvoiman uudelleenkohdentuminen" = "Labour reallocation",

  "Korkea" = "High",
  "Erittäin korkea" = "Very high",
  # figure 14

  "Tutkija" = "Doctoral level",

  "Palkkatyön kannattavuussuhde" = "Labour profitability ratio",

  # figure 18

  "Alalle tulo" = "Entry",
  "Alalta poistuminen" = "Exit",
  "Yhdysvallat" = "United States",
  "Eurooppa" = "Europe",
  "Aineelliset investoinnit" = "Tangible investment",
  "Aineettomat investoinnit" = "Intangible investment"
)

translate_levels <- function(d) {
  tr <- function(x) {
    x <- as.factor(x)
    lv <- levels(x)
    levels(x) <- coalesce(unname(fi_en[lv]), lv)
    x
  }
  mutate(d, across(any_of(c("panel", "series", "key")), tr))
}

# Pick the series of one figure. droplevels() drops the series of the other
# figures, so that the legend and the colours come only from the series of this
# figure.
luku3 <- function(fig) {
  translate_levels(droplevels(filter(dat_luku3_2026, figure == fig)))
}

luku4_2 <- function(fig) {
  translate_levels(droplevels(filter(dat_luku4_2_2026, figure == fig)))
}

luku5 <- function(fig) {
  translate_levels(droplevels(filter(dat_luku5_2026, figure == fig)))
}

luku6 <- function(fig) {
  translate_levels(droplevels(filter(dat_luku6_2026, figure == fig)))
}

# The series of figure 17 are indexed to the average of the whole period
k17_range <- range(lubridate::year(luku5("kuvio17")$time))
sub_ind_k17 <- paste0("Index, average ", k17_range[1], "–", k17_range[2], " = 100")

```

# Productivity

## GDP per capita, difference in levels

GDP relative to population. In 2020 $, adjusted for purchasing power
(log scale). Source: Eurostat, OECD, Finnish Productivity Board.

```{r}
#| label: fig-bkt-per-capita

p <- dat_gdp_main |>
  filter(time >= "1995-01-01") |>
  filter_recode(
    geo = geos,
    measure = c("GDPPOP"),
    activity = c("Total economy" = "_T"),
    price_base = c("LR"),        #
    conversion_type = c("PPP")
  ) |>
  # mutate(geo2 = suppressWarnings(fct_relevel(geo, geos, after = Inf))) |>
  # mutate(geo = fct_other(geo, keep = geos, other_level = "Other")) |>
  # filter_recode(geo = geos) |>
  select(-unit_measure) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, values, colour = geo, linewidth = geo)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = geos_colour) +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = geos_width) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = y_log_breaks) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE), linewidth = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE)) +
  the_title_blank("xyl")

save_fig(p, "1_bkt-per-capita")
save_fig_captioned(p, "1_bkt-per-capita",
  title = "GDP per capita, difference in levels",
  subtitle = "GDP relative to population. In 2020 $, adjusted for purchasing power (log scale).",
  caption = "Source: Eurostat, OECD, Finnish Productivity Board.")
save_fig_data(p, "1_bkt-per-capita", names_from = "geo")

```

Eurostat does not publish series adjusted for purchasing power, so the
conversion is made with the OECD's own conversion factors. They are not
available for every year, in which case the nearest available factor is carried
forward.

## GDP per capita, decomposition

Labour productivity and hours worked. GDP per hour worked in 2020 $, adjusted
for purchasing power, and hours worked per capita (log scale). Source: Eurostat,
OECD, Finnish Productivity Board.

```{r}
#| label: fig-bkt-per-capita-hajotelma

pdat <- dat_gdp_main |>
  filter(time >= "1995-01-01") |>
  filter_recode(
    geo = geos,
    measure = c("GDP", "HRS", "HRSPOP", "EMP", "POP", "WAP"),
    activity = c("Total economy" = "_T"),
    unit_measure = c("USD_PPP", "H", "H_PS", "PS"),
    price_base = c("LR", "_Z"),
    conversion_type = c("PPP", "_Z")
  ) |>
  select(time, geo, measure, values) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = "measure", values_from = "values") |>
  mutate(
    time = time,
    geo = geo,
    "GDP per hour worked, $" = 1000 * GDP / HRS,
    "Hours worked per capita, h" = HRS / POP,
    .keep = "none") |>
  pivot_longer(!c("time", "geo"), names_to = "measure", values_to = "values")

# the scales right in relation to the effect
rng <- pdat |>
  summarise(lo = min(values, na.rm = TRUE), hi = max(values, na.rm = TRUE), .by = measure) |>
  mutate(dec = max(log10(hi / lo)),          # the widest span in decades
         mid = sqrt(lo * hi),                # the geometric midpoint
         lo  = mid / 10^(dec / 2),
         hi  = mid * 10^(dec / 2)) |>
  select(measure, lo, hi) |>
  pivot_longer(c(lo, hi), values_to = "values") |>
  mutate(time = min(pdat$time))

p <- ggplot(pdat, aes(time, values, colour = geo, linewidth = geo)) +
  geom_blank(data = rng, aes(time, values), inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~measure, scales = "free") +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = y_log_breaks) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = geos_colour) +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = geos_width) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE), linewidth = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE)) +
  the_title_blank("xyl")

save_fig(p, "2_bkt-per-capita-hajotelma")
save_fig_captioned(p, "2_bkt-per-capita-hajotelma",
  title = "GDP per capita, decomposition",
  subtitle = paste("Labour productivity and hours worked. GDP per hour worked in 2020 $,",
                   "adjusted for purchasing power, and hours worked per capita (log scale)."),
  caption = "Source: Eurostat, OECD, Finnish Productivity Board.")
save_fig_data(p, "2_bkt-per-capita-hajotelma", names_from = c("measure", "geo"))

```

For the OECD countries, hours worked are derived back from value added and
labour productivity. The OECD replaces the national accounts hours of ten
countries with an estimate of its own, which shifts the level of hours and thus
of productivity but hardly the growth rates; see
[Työtunnit: Eurostat ja OECD](tyotunnit.qmd).

## GDP per capita, decomposition: persons employed

Labour productivity and persons employed. GDP per person employed in 2020 $,
adjusted for purchasing power, and persons employed per capita (log scale).
Source: Eurostat, OECD, Finnish Productivity Board.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
#| label: fig-bkt-per-capita-hajotelma-tyoll

pdat <- dat_gdp_main |>
  filter(time >= "1995-01-01") |>
  filter_recode(
    geo = geos,
    measure = c("GDP", "HRS", "HRSPOP", "EMP", "POP", "WAP"),
    activity = c("Total economy" = "_T"),
    unit_measure = c("USD_PPP", "H", "H_PS", "PS"),
    price_base = c("LR", "_Z"),
    conversion_type = c("PPP", "_Z")
  ) |>
  select(time, geo, measure, values) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = "measure", values_from = "values") |>
  mutate(
    time = time,
    geo = geo,
    "GDP per person employed, $" = 1000 * GDP / EMP,
    "Persons employed per capita" = EMP / POP,
    .keep = "none") |>
  pivot_longer(!c("time", "geo"), names_to = "measure", values_to = "values")

# the scales right in relation to the effect
rng <- pdat |>
  summarise(lo = min(values, na.rm = TRUE), hi = max(values, na.rm = TRUE), .by = measure) |>
  mutate(dec = max(log10(hi / lo)),          # the widest span in decades
         mid = sqrt(lo * hi),                # the geometric midpoint
         lo  = mid / 10^(dec / 2),
         hi  = mid * 10^(dec / 2)) |>
  select(measure, lo, hi) |>
  pivot_longer(c(lo, hi), values_to = "values") |>
  mutate(time = min(pdat$time))

p <- ggplot(pdat, aes(time, values, colour = geo, linewidth = geo)) +
  geom_blank(data = rng, aes(time, values), inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~measure, scales = "free") +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = y_log_breaks) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = geos_colour) +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = geos_width) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE), linewidth = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE)) +
  the_title_blank("xyl")

save_fig(p, "bkt-per-capita-hajotelma_tyoll")

```

## Labour productivity growth in the business sector

Labour productivity, value added per hour worked. Business sector, index
2007 = 100 (log scale). Source: Eurostat, OECD, Finnish Productivity Board.

```{r}
#| label: fig-tuottavuus-yrityssektori

p <- dat_gva_ind_comb |>
  select(-source) |>
  filter(time >= "1995-01-01") |>
  filter_recode(
    measure = c("GVAHRS"),
    activity = c("Business sector" = "BTNXL"),
    vars = c("fp_2020_lc")
  ) |>
  mutate(values = rebase(values, time, baseyear = 2007), .by = where(is.factor)) |>
  # filter(geo != "DK") |>
  filter_recode(
    geo = geos
  ) |>

  ggplot(aes(time, values, colour = geo, linewidth = geo)) +
  # facet_wrap(~ activity, nrow = 1) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = geos_colour) +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = geos_width) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = y_log_breaks) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE), linewidth = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE)) +
  the_title_blank("xyl")

save_fig(p, "3_tuottavuus-yrityssektori")
save_fig_captioned(p, "3_tuottavuus-yrityssektori",
  title = "Labour productivity in the business sector",
  subtitle = "Value added per hour worked. Business sector, index 2007 = 100, log scale",
  caption = "Source: Eurostat, OECD, Finnish Productivity Board.")
save_fig_data(p, "3_tuottavuus-yrityssektori", names_from = "geo")

```

The business sector is NACE B–N excluding real estate (L). For the Eurostat
countries it is summed from the A\*10 industries through series in the previous
year's prices and chained again; for the OECD countries it comes ready from the
database (`BTNXL`). The series are in national currency, so the figure shows
growth, not differences in levels.

## Labour productivity growth in industry and in services

Labour productivity by industry, value added per hour worked. Index
2007 = 100 (log scale). Source: Eurostat, OECD, Finnish Productivity Board.

```{r}
#| label: fig-tuottavuus-toimialat

p <- dat_gva_ind_comb|>
  select(-source) |>
  filter(time >= "2000-01-01") |>
  filter_recode(
    measure = c("GVAHRS"),
    activity = c("Industry" = "BTE", "Construction" = "F","Private services" = "GTNXL"),
    vars = c("fp_2020_lc")
  ) |>
  mutate(values = rebase(values, time, baseyear = 2007), .by = where(is.factor)) |>
  filter(geo != "DK") |>
  filter_recode(
    geo = geos
  ) |>

  ggplot(aes(time, values, colour = geo, linewidth = geo)) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(60, 150), breaks = y_log_breaks) +
  facet_wrap(~ activity) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = geos_colour) +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = geos_width) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE), linewidth = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE)) +
  the_title_blank("xyl")

save_fig(p, "4_tuottavuus-toimialat")
save_fig_captioned(p, "4_tuottavuus-toimialat",
  title = "Labour productivity growth in industry and in services",
  subtitle = "Labour productivity by industry, value added per hour worked. Index 2007 = 100 (log scale).",
  caption = "Source: Eurostat, OECD, Finnish Productivity Board.")
save_fig_data(p, "4_tuottavuus-toimialat", names_from = c("activity", "geo"))

```


In the OECD's industry data, industry (B–E) covers manufacturing only, which
applies to the countries that come from the OECD; see
[Talouskasvu ja tuottavuus](main.qmd).

## The level of productivity in services

Labour productivity in services, value added per hour worked in 2017 $, adjusted
for purchasing power (log scale). Source: Eurostat, OECD, Finnish Productivity
Board.

```{r}
#| label: fig-tuottavuustaso-palvelut

# The figure as it is in the Word version of the report: France is left out, so
# the countries and their colours are those of geos_s1, and the text is of the
# size 12 (theme_fpb()'s default) instead of the 11 of the rest of the figures.
geos_s1 <- geos[geos != "FR"]
geos_s1_width <- set_names(if_else(geos_s1 %in% c("FI"), 2, 1.3), names(geos_s1))
geos_s1_colour <- set_names(c("grey80", rev(ggcustom_pal(length(geos_s1) - 1, "fpb"))), names(geos_s1))

p <- dat_gva_ind_comb |> 
  filter(time >= "1995-01-01") |> 
  filter_recode(
    measure = c("GVAHRS"),
    activity = c("Private services" = "GTNXL"),
    vars = c("fp_2020_ppp17")
  ) |> 
  # mutate(values = rebase(values, time, baseyear = 2007), .by = where(is.factor)) |> 
  filter_recode(
    geo = geos_s1
  ) |> 
  ggplot(aes(time, values, colour = geo, linewidth = geo)) +
  theme_fpb(base_size = 12) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(50, 150), breaks = y_log_breaks) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = geos_s1_colour) +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = geos_s1_width) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = y_log_breaks) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE), linewidth = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE)) +
  the_title_blank("xyl") 

save_fig(p, "s1_tuottavuustaso-palvelut")
save_fig_captioned(p, "s1_tuottavuustaso-palvelut",
  title = "The level of productivity in services",
  subtitle = "Value added per hour worked, in 2017 $ adjusted for purchasing power, log scale",
  caption = "Source: Eurostat, OECD, Finnish Productivity Board.")
save_fig_data(p, "s1_tuottavuustaso-palvelut", names_from = "geo")

```

# Developments in cost competitiveness

## Unit cost indicators

Finland's relative unit labour costs with different definitions. `r sub_ind`.
Source: Eurostat, Finnish Productivity Board.

```{r}
#| label: fig-ulc-maaritelmat

p <- pick(c("Nominal, national currency" = "nulc_aper",
            "Nominal, common currency" = "nulc_aper_eur",
            "Nominal, terms of trade adjusted" = "nulc_aper_eur_atot",
            "Real" = "rulc_aper")) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, values, colour = vars)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 100, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line() +
  the_title_blank("xl") +
  the_legend_bot() +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +
  labs(y = NULL)

save_fig(p, "5_ulc-maaritelmat")
save_fig_captioned(p, "5_ulc-maaritelmat",
  title = "Unit cost indicators",
  subtitle = sub_ind,
  caption = "Source: Eurostat, OECD, Finnish Productivity Board.")
save_fig_data(p, "5_ulc-maaritelmat", names_from = "vars")


```

The ratio is calculated against 17 peer countries, except for the terms of trade
adjusted one, which is only among the 15 Eurostat countries: the OECD
productivity database has neither exports nor imports. The last years of the USA
and Japan have been extended with the growth rates of the OECD's quarterly
series, so the last year rests partly on extended data (the `extended` column).

## Decomposition of the ULC

The components of the relative unit labour cost. `r sub_ind`. Source: Eurostat,
Finnish Productivity Board.

```{r}
#| label: fig-ulc-hajotelma

p <- pick(c("Productivity" = "lp_ind",
            "Compensation per employee" = "d1_per_ind",
            "Exchange rate" = "exch_eur_ind")) |>
  mutate(values = if_else(vars == "Exchange rate", 100^2 / values, values)) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, values, colour = vars)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 100, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line() +
  the_title_blank("xl") +
  the_legend_bot() +
  labs(y = NULL)

save_fig(p, "6_ulc-hajotelma")
save_fig_captioned(p, "6_ulc-hajotelma",
  title = "Decomposition of the ULC",
  subtitle = paste0("The components of the relative unit labour cost. ", sub_ind, "."),
  caption = "Source: Eurostat, Finnish Productivity Board.")
save_fig_data(p, "6_ulc-hajotelma", names_from = "vars")

```

The exchange rate index is national currency per euro, so a rise means that the
currency weakens. In the figure it is turned upside down (100² / index), so that
a rise is a strengthening of the currency and thus a rise in the unit labour
cost in a common currency. A rise in compensation per employee raises the unit
labour cost, a rise in productivity lowers it.

# Figures of chapter 4

# Productivity in the public sector

The public sector here is three industries together: public administration,
education, and human health and social work activities (NACE O–Q). They also
include, especially health services, production by the private sector, because
there is no comprehensive data for a country comparison with a split by sector
alone. The industries separately and a version based on the OECD data alone are
in the article [Julkisen sektorin tuottavuus](public.qmd) (in Finnish).

## Productivity in the public sector

Labour productivity in the public sector, value added per hour worked in 2020 $,
adjusted for purchasing power. Index, 2000 = 100. Source: Eurostat, OECD,
Finnish Productivity Board.

```{r}
#| label: fig-tuottavuus-julkinen


p <- dat_gva_ind_comb |>
  filter(time >= "1980-01-01") |>
  filter_recode(
    measure = c("GVAHRS"),
    activity = c("Public sector" = "OTQ"),
    vars = c("fp_2020_ppp17")
  ) |>
  mutate(values = rebase(values, time, baseyear = 2000), .by = where(is.factor)) |>
  filter(geo != "DK") |>
  filter_recode(
    geo = geos
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, values, colour = geo, linewidth = geo)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = geos_colour) +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = geos_width) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE), linewidth = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE)) +
  the_title_blank("xyl")

save_fig(p, "12_tuottavuus-julkinen")
save_fig_captioned(p, "12_tuottavuus-julkinen",
  title = "Productivity in the public sector",
  subtitle = paste("Labour productivity in the public sector, value added per hour worked in 2020 $,",
                   "adjusted for purchasing power. Index, 2000 = 100."),
  caption = "Source: Eurostat, OECD, Finnish Productivity Board.")
save_fig_data(p, "12_tuottavuus-julkinen", names_from = "geo")

```

The Eurostat data is retrieved at the A\*10 level of NACE, where public
administration, education, and human health and social work activities are one
industry (`OTQ`); for the OECD countries the same whole is summed from
industries. The adjustment for purchasing power is made by industry and is
based on the price level of 2017, so the figure compares growth, not levels.

## Productivity growth with and without the public sector

Average annual growth of labour productivity in the whole economy, in the public
sector and excluding the public sector, and the difference between the growth
rates of the whole economy and of the economy excluding the public sector.
Average over `r public_period_lab`, %. Source: Eurostat, OECD, Finnish
Productivity Board.

```{r}
#| label: fig-tuottavuuskasvu-julkinen

# Chain-linked volumes are not additive, so the public sector is subtracted from
# the total economy through series in the previous year's prices and the
# difference is chained again. Hours worked are additive and are subtracted as
# they are.
pdat <- dat_gva_ind_comb |>
  filter(time >= "1995-01-01") |>
  filter_recode(
    measure = c("GVA", "HRS"),
    activity = c("TOT" = "_T", "OTQ"),
    vars = c("cp", "fp_2020_lc")
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(measure, vars), values_from = values, names_sep = "__") |>
  select(-HRS__fp_2020_lc) |>
  mutate(GVA__pp = prev_year_prices(GVA__cp, GVA__fp_2020_lc, time), .by = c(geo, activity)) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = activity,
    values_from = where(is.numeric),
    names_sep = "___"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    GVA__cp___TOTex = GVA__cp___TOT - GVA__cp___OTQ,
    HRS__cp___TOTex = HRS__cp___TOT - HRS__cp___OTQ,
    GVA__pp___TOTex = GVA__pp___TOT - GVA__pp___OTQ
  ) |>
  mutate(GVA__fp_2020_lc___TOTex = fixed_prices(GVA__cp___TOTex, GVA__pp___TOTex, time, 2020), .by = geo) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = where(is.numeric), names_to = c("vars", "activity"), names_sep = "___",
               values_to = "values", names_transform = as_factor) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = "vars", values_from = "values") |>
  mutate(GVAHRS__fp_2020_lc = GVA__fp_2020_lc / HRS__cp) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = where(is.numeric), names_to = c("measure", "vars"), names_sep = "__",
               values_to = "values", names_transform = as_factor)

p <- pdat |>
  filter_recode(
    measure = "GVAHRS",
    vars = "fp_2020_lc",
    geo = geos
  ) |>
  mutate(values = pc(values, 1, time), .by = c(geo, activity)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = activity, values_from = values) |>
  mutate(diff = TOT - TOTex) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = where(is.numeric), names_to = "activity", values_to = "values",
               names_transform = as_factor) |>
  filter_recode(
    activity =
      c("Total economy" = "TOT",
        "Public sector" = "OTQ",
        "Excluding public sector" = "TOTex",
        "Difference" = "diff")
  ) |>
  filter(year(time) %in% public_period) |>
  summarise(values = mean(values), .by = c(geo, activity)) |>
  mutate(geo = fct_reorder(geo, values, .fun = max)) |>
  ggplot(aes(geo, values, fill = activity)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(n.dodge = 2)) +
  the_title_blank("xyl")

save_fig(p, "13_tuottavuuskasvu-julkinen")
save_fig_captioned(p, "13_tuottavuuskasvu-julkinen",
  title = "Productivity growth with and without the public sector",
  subtitle = paste0(
    "Average annual growth of labour productivity in the whole economy, in the public ",
    "sector and excluding the public sector, and the difference between the growth ",
    "rates of the whole economy and of the economy excluding the public sector. ",
    "Average over ", public_period_lab, ", %."),
  caption = "Source: Eurostat, OECD, Finnish Productivity Board.")
save_fig_data(p, "13_tuottavuuskasvu-julkinen", names_from = "activity")

```

The difference tells how much the public sector has slowed down (a negative
number) or sped up the productivity growth of the whole economy compared with an
economy from which the public sector has been removed. The average is
calculated without any correction for missing years, so a country is left out of
the figure if even one year of the period is missing. Value added excluding the
public sector has been chained again to 2020 prices in national currency; see
[Talouskasvu ja tuottavuus](main.qmd).

## Human capital stock

The development of the human capital stock in three forecast scenarios in
2024–2075. EUR million, volume, reference year 2015. Sources: Statistics
Finland, calculations by Arto Kokkinen (National Audit Office of Finland) and
Pirkka Jalasjoki (Bank of Finland).

```{r}
#| label: fig-inhimillinen-paaomakanta

# The legend texts of the sheet are the name of the scenario and its definition,
# separated by a colon. The legend has the name and the definitions are below
# the figure, because the whole texts would take half of the height of the
# figure.

lines <- c("Unchanged", "Baseline", "Optimistic")

p <- luku4_2("kuvio16") |>
  mutate(values = values / 1000) |>
  mutate(vars = fct_rev(as_factor(series))) %>%{
  ggplot(droplevels(filter(., !(vars %in% lines))), aes(time, values, fill = vars)) +
  geom_area() +
  geom_line(data = (filter(., vars %in% lines)), aes(time, values, colour = vars, fill = NULL)) +
  the_title_blank("xyl") +
      the_legend_bot() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = rev(c("grey25", "grey50", "grey75"))) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
      guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(colour = NA), nrow = 3), colour = guide_legend(nrow = 3)) +
      theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())}

save_fig(p, "16_inhimillinen-paaomakanta")
save_fig_captioned(p, "16_inhimillinen-paaomakanta",
  title = "Human capital stock",
  subtitle = paste("The development of the human capital stock in three forecast scenarios in 2024–2075.",
                   "EUR million, volume, reference year 2015."),
  caption = "Sources: Statistics Finland, calculations by Arto Kokkinen (National Audit Office of Finland) and Pirkka Jalasjoki (Bank of Finland).")
# p$data is only the part of the stacked scenarios (the line series are the data
# of the layer of their own geom_line()), so only they are saved in the wide
# file
save_fig_data(p, "16_inhimillinen-paaomakanta", names_from = "vars")

```

In the baseline scenario 50 % of those aged 25–34 have a tertiary degree by
2035 and in the optimistic scenario 70 % by 2040. The scenarios differ from each
other only from 2024, so before that the lines overlap. The sheet also has the
capital stock of the baseline scenario by level of education, which the figure
does not use. Description of the method: Kokkinen, A., Obstbaum, M., and
Mäki-Fränti P. (2021). Bank of Finland's Long-Run Forecast Framework with Human
Capital. BoF Economics Review 10-2021.

# Figures of chapter 5

The series of chapter 5 do not come from statistical interfaces but ready
calculated from the Excel file `data-raw/rap_2026/Luku5.xlsx`, which has one
sheet per figure and on every sheet also a model figure. The sheets are read
into one long table by the script `data-raw/read_luku5.R`, which has to be run
before this document is rendered.

From the model figures we have taken which series are in the figure, the legends
of the series and the titles of the panels of figure 20. Otherwise the figures
are in the same style as the other figures of the report: the title, subtitle
and source are text above the figure and every figure is also saved as a png and
a pdf.

## Labour productivity and real wages

Labour productivity and real wages at value added prices. Index, 2000 = 100,
quarterly. Source: Finnish Productivity Board's own calculations.

```{r}
#| label: fig-tuottavuus-reaalipalkat

p <- luku5("kuvio16") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, values, colour = series)) +
```

```{r}

  mutate(series = fct_recode(series, "Aggregate level" = "Business sector level")) |>
```

## Firm level and creative destruction by technology level

Productivity developments by technology level, at the level of firms and through
creative destruction. Percentage points, 1995 = 0. Source: Finnish Productivity
Board's own calculations.

```{r}
#| label: fig-luova-tuho-teknologia

df <- luku5("kuvio20")

span <- max(tapply(df$values, df$panel, \(v) diff(range(v)))) * 1.05

rajat <- df |>
  group_by(panel, series) |>
  reframe(time = min(time),
          values = mean(range(values)) + c(-1, 1) * span / 2)


p <- luku5("kuvio20") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, values, colour = series)) +
  facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_width(10)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line() +
  ggh4x::facetted_pos_scales(
    y = list(scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-60, 10)),
             scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 70)))
  )  +
  # geom_blank(data = rajat) +
  the_title_blank("xyl") +
  the_legend_bot() +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2))

save_fig(p, "21_luova-tuho-teknologia")
save_fig_captioned(p, "21_luova-tuho-teknologia",
  title = "Firm level and creative destruction by technology level",
  subtitle = paste("Productivity developments by technology level, at the level of firms and through",
                   "creative destruction. Percentage points, 1995 = 0."),
  caption = "Source: Finnish Productivity Board's own calculations.")
save_fig_data(p, "21_luova-tuho-teknologia", names_from = c("panel", "series"))

```

The titles of the panels and the legends of the series are from the model
figures. The panels have the same scale, because both are in the same unit and
comparing their magnitudes is the point of the figure; the model figures are two
separate figures with scales of their own.

## The divergence component and the change in dispersion

The effect of the divergence component (left axis) and the change in the
dispersion of productivity (right axis), observed and HP-filtered series.
Source: Finnish Productivity Board's own calculations.

```{r}
#| label: fig-divergenssi-hajonta

# The series of the right axis are drawn on the left axis shrunk to a fifth, and
# the right axis multiplies them back. This way zero is at the same place on both
# axes; in the model figure the axes are not aligned at zero.
k21_oikea <- c("Change in dispersion (right axis)")
k21_suhde <- 5

p <- luku5("kuvio21") |>
  separate_wider_delim(series, delim = ", ", names = c("series", "type"),
                       too_few = "align_start") |>
  mutate(series = as_factor(series),
         series = fct_recode(series,
           "Divergence component (left axis)" = "Divergence component",
           "Change in dispersion (right axis)" = "Change in dispersion")) |>

  mutate(
    type = if_else(is.na(type), "Original", "HP-filtered"),
    type = as_factor(type)) |>
  mutate(values = if_else(series %in% k21_oikea, values / k21_suhde, values)) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, values, colour = series, linewidth = type)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(0.5,2), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 10),
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . * k21_suhde, breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 10))
  ) +
  the_title_blank("xyl") +
  the_legend_bot() +
  # the legends are long, so one column fits the width of the figure
  guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 1))

save_fig(p, "22_divergenssi-hajonta")
save_fig_captioned(p, "22_divergenssi-hajonta",
  title = "The divergence component and the change in dispersion",
  subtitle = paste("The effect of the divergence component (left axis) and the change in the",
                   "dispersion of productivity (right axis), observed and HP-filtered series."),
  caption = "Source: Finnish Productivity Board's own calculations.")
save_fig_data(p, "22_divergenssi-hajonta", names_from = c("series", "type"))

```

The right axis is five times the left one. The series of the change in
dispersion lack the first year, because they are changes.

# Figures of chapter 6

As those of chapters 3 and 5, the series of chapter 6 come ready calculated from
the Excel file `data-raw/rap_2026/Luku6.xlsx`, which has one sheet per figure.
The workbook has been put together from the individual data point files that came
with the manuscript of chapter 6; the sheet Sisältö (contents) has the titles of
the figures and the source files. The sheets are read by the script
`data-raw/read_luku6.R`, which has to be run before this document is rendered.

The model figures are in the manuscript of chapter 6, not in the workbook. From
them we have taken which series are in the figure, the legends of the series and
the titles of the panels; the titles and the sources are the captions of the
manuscript.

## Industry concentration in the EU countries

The development of industry concentration in different EU countries. CR4 share,
%. Source: based on figures of Anttinen et al. (2026) and Calligaris et al.
(2024).

```{r}
#| label: fig-keskittyminen-eu

# Finland and Europe separately, the other countries as one grey group as in the
# model
k23_colour <- set_names(c("grey80", ggcustom_pal(2, "fpb")),
                        c("Other countries", "Finland", "Europe (GDP-weighted)"))
k23_width <- set_names(c(0.6, 2, 1.3), names(k23_colour))

p <- luku6("kuvio23") |>
  # the countries are drawn in the order of the series, so that Finland and
  # Europe come on top of the grey lines
  mutate(key = fct_reorder(key, as.integer(series))) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, values, colour = series, linewidth = series, group = key)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = k23_colour) +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = k23_width) +
  the_title_blank("xyl") +
  the_legend_bot()

save_fig(p, "23_keskittyminen-eu")
save_fig_captioned(p, "23_keskittyminen-eu",
  title = "Industry concentration in the EU countries",
  subtitle = "The development of industry concentration in different EU countries. CR4 share, %.",
  caption = "Source: based on figures of Anttinen et al. (2026) and Calligaris et al. (2024).")
# key is country specific, series only groups (many countries share the same
# "Other countries" series), so the widening is done by key
save_fig_data(p, "23_keskittyminen-eu", names_from = "key")

```

The grey lines are Belgium, Denmark, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Italy,
Norway, Poland, Portugal, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden and the United Kingdom. The
CR4 share is the share of the four largest firms of an industry, and the figures
by country are averages calculated over industries.

## Concentration indices of industries in Finland

Concentration indices of industries in Finland in 2014–2024. HHI index and CR4
share, %. Source: Anttinen et al. (2026).

```{r}
#| label: fig-keskittymisindeksit

p <- luku6("kuvio24") |>
  mutate(panel = fct_recode(panel, "CR4, %" = "CR4")) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, values, linetype = series)) +
  facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free_y") +
  geom_line() +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(1, 3, 3)) +
  scale_y_continuous(n.breaks = 8) +
  expand_limits(y = 0) +
  the_title_blank("xyl") +
  the_legend_bot()

save_fig(p, "24_keskittymisindeksit")
save_fig_captioned(p, "24_keskittymisindeksit",
  title = "Concentration indices of industries in Finland",
  subtitle = "Concentration indices of industries in Finland in 2014–2024. HHI index and CR4 share, %.",
  caption = "Source: Anttinen et al. (2026).")
save_fig_data(p, "24_keskittymisindeksit", names_from = c("panel", "series"))

```

The scales of the panels are in different units, the HHI in index points and the
CR4 in per cent, so they have scales of their own. The HHI is the sum of the
squares of the market shares of the firms of an industry and takes values
between 0 and 10,000; p25 and p75 are the lower and upper quartile limits of the
distribution of industries.
